word-counter.title: Word Counter
word-counter.shortDesc: Count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs in your text.

seo.title: Word Counter - Instant, Private Counting
seo.description: Count words, characters and sentences with this free word counter as you type. Check a character count against your limit, then copy your stats.

word-counter.emptyHint: Nothing to count yet. Paste text or try the sample.
word-counter.inputHint: Your text stays on this device.
word-counter.shortcutHint: Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + C copies the stats

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: Word Counter counts words, characters, sentences, paragraphs and lines as you type or paste text. Everything happens in your browser, so your writing never leaves the device. You get instant, exact results with no sign-up, no upload and no waiting.
page.contextualLink: Need to change the case of the same text? Try {tool}.
page.whatIs:
A word counter is a small tool that reads a piece of text and reports how many words, characters, sentences, paragraphs and lines it contains. It removes the manual work of selecting text and guessing at length, which matters when an editor, form or submission sets a strict limit.

Most counters split words on whitespace: any run of letters or numbers between spaces becomes one word. That is why a hyphenated term such as well-known counts as one word in most tools, while well known counts as two. Punctuation attached to a word does not create a new word. Character counts usually include spaces, so a 200-word paragraph may contain well over 1,000 characters.

Sentence detection looks for full stops, question marks and exclamation marks. Paragraph detection looks for a blank line between blocks. Line counts follow line breaks, not visual wrapping, so a long line that wraps on screen is still one line. Reading time is an estimate based on an average adult speed of 200 words per minute; it is a guide, not a promise about how fast you will read.

Word counts also behave differently across scripts. Languages such as English use spaces to separate words, while Chinese, Japanese and Korean do not. A whitespace-based counter will report very few words for those languages even though the text is long. Use the character count instead when working with scripts that do not use spaces.
page.howTo:
Paste or type your text into the input box on the left.
Read the live counts in the result panel on the right.
Try sample to see every count update with ready-made text.
Copy the full set of counts when you need to share or record it.
Clear the box to start again with a new piece of text.
page.exampleInput: Hello world. This is a test.
page.exampleOutput:
Word count: 6
Characters: 28
Characters (no spaces): 23
Sentences: 2
Paragraphs: 1
Lines: 1
Reading time: 1 min
Speaking time: 1 min
page.exampleNote: The numbers match the counting rules used by the tool above.
page.features:
Live counts::Every number updates as soon as you type or paste.
Seven measures::Words, characters, characters without spaces, sentences, paragraphs, lines and reading time.
Copy stats::Copy all counts as plain text in one click.
Try sample::Fill the box with sample text to see the tool working.
Private by design::All counting happens in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
page.useCases:
Meet an assignment limit::Check an essay or blog draft before you submit it.
Plan a blog post::See whether an introduction is too long or too short.
Check form input::Verify text before pasting it into a field with a character cap.
Review translations::Compare the length of two versions of the same paragraph.
page.mistakes:
Ignoring spaces::Character counts include spaces. Use the no-spaces count when a form excludes them.
Pasting from PDFs::Copied text can carry hard line breaks that inflate the line count. Check the text before relying on it.
Mixing line endings::Windows and Unix line endings both count as one line here, but pasted content may include extra blank lines.
page.limits:
Very long text can be slow on older phones.
Word counts for scripts without spaces are approximate.
Reading time assumes 200 words per minute and is only an estimate.
page.faqs:
Does Word Counter count spaces as characters?::Yes. Characters includes spaces and punctuation; use Characters (no spaces) if the form ignores whitespace.
How does the tool count a word?::Each run of non-whitespace characters is one word. Hyphens stay joined and attached punctuation adds no word.
Will my text be uploaded?::No. Counting happens in your browser; nothing is uploaded or stored after you close the tab.
Why is my word count different in another editor?::Editors differ on hyphens, numbers and symbols. This tool counts by whitespace, so check the form's own rule.
Does it work for Chinese or Japanese text?::Characters, lines and paragraphs work well. Word counts need spaces, so use the character count for Chinese, Japanese or Korean.
Is reading time accurate?::It's an estimate at 200 words per minute, not a measure of your pace. Use it to compare drafts.
page.trustBody: Built by the Toolpika team. This page describes the counting rules used by the tool above. Last updated 24 November 2026.

case-converter.title: Case Converter
case-converter.shortDesc: Convert text to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case or camelCase.

seo.title: Case Converter - Seven Text Styles in One Click
seo.description: Change text between uppercase, lowercase and title case with this case converter. Need camelCase or snake_case for code? Paste your text and pick a style.

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: Case Converter rewrites pasted text into seven styles, including UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case and camelCase. Choose a style button and read the result instantly. The conversion runs in your browser, so your text stays on this device with no account needed.
page.contextualLink: Want a quick count of the converted text before you paste it back? Use {tool}.
page.whatIs:
A case converter rewrites the same characters into a different capitalisation or naming pattern. It never changes the meaning of your words; it changes how they look, so they fit a style guide, a programming convention or a form that expects a certain format.

UPPERCASE raises every letter, lowercase lowers every letter, and Title Case capitalises the start of each word after a space or hyphen. Sentence case capitalises the first letter of a sentence and leaves the rest lowercase. These styles keep your punctuation and spacing exactly where you put them.

Identifier styles work differently. camelCase joins words with no separator and capitalises every word after the first. kebab-case uses hyphens, and snake_case uses underscores. All three split input on anything that is not a letter or number, so commas and full stops disappear from the result.

Case matters in code and data. JavaScript variables are case-sensitive, so userName and username can be different names. Many configuration files use lowercase keys, while headings use Title Case. Converting early avoids inconsistent labels later. Unicode letters work in the style functions, but scripts without a clear upper and lower form will not change. The tool offers seven styles in total, covering the common options without a settings panel.
page.howTo:
Paste or type text into the Text box.
Choose a style button such as UPPERCASE, Title Case or camelCase.
Read the converted text in the Result box.
Pick another style to compare outputs without retyping.
Copy the result or Clear both boxes to start over.
page.exampleLabel: Title Case from a plain phrase
page.exampleNote: Any style button produces a different result from the same input.
page.features:
Seven styles::UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, camelCase, kebab-case and snake_case.
One-click output::Each style button replaces the Result text immediately.
Side-by-side panels::Input stays on the left and output on the right.
Copy and clear::Copy the result or reset both boxes in one click.
No uploads::Conversion runs entirely inside your browser tab.
page.useCases:
Prepare code identifiers::Turn a phrase into camelCase, kebab-case or snake_case.
Polish headings::Use Title Case or Sentence case on a draft.
Match a style guide::Convert pasted copy before sending it to an editor.
Normalise imported data::Make mixed-case labels consistent in a spreadsheet.
page.mistakes:
Expecting punctuation removal::Title and sentence case keep punctuation; choose an identifier style to drop it.
Using camelCase for display text::camelCase strips spaces; use Title Case for headings.
Picking a style twice::Each button overwrites the previous result, so compare before you copy.
page.limits:
Seven output styles are available; there are no custom rules.
Very long text may be slow to redraw on older phones.
Punctuation is not removed from title or sentence case.
page.faqs:
Which style should I use for a variable name?::Use camelCase or snake_case for code identifiers. camelCase joins words without separators and capitalises each later word, while snake_case uses underscores. Both come from the same input, so try each button and copy the one your project convention expects.
Does Title Case capitalise every word?::It capitalises the first letter of each word separated by spaces or hyphens and lowercases everything else. Short words such as of still receive a capital here, so check your house style if it keeps those words lowercase.
What happens to punctuation in camelCase?::Word splitting removes punctuation because identifiers are built from letters and numbers only. A phrase like Hello, world! becomes helloWorld. If you need the punctuation preserved, choose UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case or Sentence case instead.
Can I convert text in another language?::The style functions use Unicode letter categories, so accented letters and many scripts are handled. Camel, kebab and snake styles join words using letters and numbers from any script. Read the result before using it in code that expects ASCII only.
Can I compare two styles at once?::You can compare them one after another: click a style, read the Result box, then click another. Each button replaces the previous output rather than adding a second column. Copy the version you want before trying the next style.
Is this case converter free and private?::Yes. The tool is free to use, needs no account and runs inside your browser. Your text is not uploaded or stored, and closing the tab clears it. That makes it suitable for drafts and identifiers you would rather keep on your own device.
page.trustBody: Written by the Toolpika team. The seven styles listed here match the buttons on the page above. Reviewed 24 November 2026.

image-compressor.title: Image Compressor
image-compressor.shortDesc: Compress JPEG and PNG images locally in your browser.

seo.title: Image Compressor - Shrink JPEG and PNG Files
seo.description: Shrink photos with this image compressor that runs on your device. Adjust JPEG quality, compare sizes, then download the smaller file.

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: Image Compressor shrinks JPEG, PNG and WebP files by re-encoding them on a canvas inside your browser. Set a quality level, compare the saved size and download a JPEG. Your image is never uploaded, and no sign-up is needed to get started.
page.contextualLink: If an image sits beside a long caption, check that caption's length with {tool}.
page.whatIs:
An image compressor reduces the number of bytes needed to store a picture. This tool does that by drawing your file onto a canvas and exporting it again as JPEG at a chosen quality, all inside your browser.

Quality is a number from 10 to 90 percent. Lower values discard more detail and usually produce a smaller file; higher values keep more of the original texture. Each change re-encodes the image, so you can compare the Original, Compressed and Saved figures before you download. The preview shows the re-encoded picture at a glance.

JPEG has no alpha channel. When a PNG with transparency is encoded, transparent pixels are flattened onto white. The tool also caps the longest side at 4096 pixels, which keeps very large photos manageable without changing their aspect ratio.

Files above 20 MB are rejected before decoding. Accepted input formats are JPEG, PNG and WebP; the output is always a JPEG named with -compressed.jpg. Compression is lossy, so repeated saves degrade detail. Keep the original file if you may need it later.

Because encoding happens locally, the image is never uploaded to a server. That makes the tool useful for screenshots, product photos and personal pictures you would rather not send elsewhere.
page.howTo:
Choose an image or drop a JPEG, PNG or WebP file onto the drop zone.
Move the Quality slider between 10 and 90 percent.
Compare Original, Compressed and Saved sizes in the result panel.
Download the JPEG when the size looks right.
Clear the file to try another image.
page.exampleOutput:
Original: 100.0 KB
Compressed: 25.0 KB
Saved: 75%
Download: photo-compressed.jpg
page.exampleNote: Sizes are illustrative; your result depends on the image content.
page.features:
Local processing::Your file never leaves the browser tab.
Quality slider::Set JPEG quality from 10 to 90 percent in five-point steps.
Size comparison::See Original, Compressed and Saved values after each encode.
Preview::Check the re-encoded image before downloading.
Download name::Saved file uses the original name with -compressed.jpg.
File limit::Images above 20 MB show an error before processing.
page.useCases:
Shrink page assets::Reduce a JPEG before uploading it to a site.
Prepare email attachments::Lower the file size before sending.
Speed up shared photos::Compress a picture for a chat or forum post.
Fit an upload limit::Adjust quality until the file meets a size cap.
page.mistakes:
Raising quality for tiny files::Higher quality can increase output size; compare the Saved figure.
Expecting PNG output::Images are always re-encoded as JPEG with a white background.
Compressing an already small file::Re-encoding may produce a larger file; check before downloading.
page.limits:
Files larger than 20 MB are rejected before processing.
Output is always JPEG, so PNG transparency becomes white.
The longest side is capped at 4096 pixels.
The Quality slider runs from 10 to 90 percent.
page.faqs:
Why is my compressed image still large?::Some images contain detail that survives JPEG re-encoding well. Lower the Quality slider in five-point steps and watch the Saved figure. If the file barely shrinks, the original may already be efficient or very small.
Can I keep PNG transparency?::No. Output is always JPEG, which has no alpha channel, so transparent areas become white. Use a different workflow if you must preserve transparency, such as an image format that supports alpha or a dedicated PNG optimiser.
What does the Quality slider change?::It sets the JPEG encoder quality from 10 to 90 percent. Higher values keep more detail but produce larger files; lower values shrink more and can add visible artifacts. The tool re-encodes at the chosen value every time you move the slider.
Why is there a 20 MB limit?::Files above 20 MB are rejected before decoding so the page stays responsive on ordinary devices. The check happens locally, and you see a short error message. Split large batches into smaller files or resize the source before trying again.
What is the file name of the download?::The download keeps your original name, drops its extension and appends -compressed.jpg. For example, a source called photo.png produces photo-compressed.jpg. The preview above the download shows the result before you save it.
Does this compressor upload my photos?::No uploads occur. Reading, resizing and encoding all happen in your browser tab with a canvas. Nothing is sent to a server, and closing or refreshing the page releases the temporary preview. Use it for personal photos without creating an account.
page.trustBody: Maintained by the Toolpika team. The 20 MB limit and JPEG output match the tool above. Updated 24 November 2026.

json-formatter.title: JSON Formatter
json-formatter.shortDesc: Format, validate and minify JSON in your browser.

seo.title: JSON Formatter - Pretty Print and Validate Fast
seo.description: Clean up messy data with this JSON formatter that checks syntax as you work. Minify JSON for smaller payloads or fix errors, then copy the result.

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: JSON Formatter checks and reformats JSON text in your browser. Click Format for two-space indentation or Minify for a compact result, and read the parser message if the input is broken. No upload, account or waiting is needed to clean up your text.
page.contextualLink: When a JSON field holds a long description, check its length with {tool}.
page.whatIs:
A JSON formatter takes JSON text and rewrites it with consistent indentation and line breaks. The underlying data stays the same; only the whitespace changes, which makes the structure easier to read and review.

JSON stands for JavaScript Object Notation. It stores data as objects with key-value pairs, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null. Keys and string values must use double quotes. Comments, trailing commas and single quotes are not part of the format, so a parser rejects them.

This tool parses the input first. If parsing succeeds, Format writes the result with two spaces of indentation and Minify writes it without optional whitespace. If parsing fails, the result stays empty and the parser message appears in the panel.

Formatting helps when you inspect an API response, check a configuration file or prepare a request body. Minifying helps when a payload needs to be compact. Key order is preserved from the parsed text. The tool checks syntax, not meaning: it does not validate against a schema or verify that a value has the expected type. Both buttons use the same parser, so they accept and reject exactly the same input. The result pane stays read-only so the source text remains the only thing you edit.
page.howTo:
Paste JSON into the Text box on the left.
Click Format to pretty print the structure with two-space indentation.
Click Minify to remove optional whitespace instead.
Fix the input if the tool reports Invalid JSON.
Copy the valid output when it looks right.
page.exampleNote: Two-space indentation is what the Format button writes.
page.features:
Format button::Pretty prints with two-space indentation.
Minify button::Removes optional whitespace from valid JSON.
Validation::Invalid JSON shows the parser message instead of a result.
Valid badge::Confirms the output parsed successfully.
Copy::Takes the exact formatted text to your clipboard.
Monospace editors::Input and output use a fixed-width font for alignment.
page.useCases:
Inspect API responses::Pretty print a compact payload to read its structure.
Debug a failed request::Spot syntax errors before sending JSON.
Reduce payload size::Minify JSON for a test request.
Clean pasted config::Reformat a settings block copied from a log.
page.mistakes:
Pasting wrapped or truncated JSON::Missing brackets fail parsing; copy the full object.
Assuming Minify validates differently::Both buttons use the same parser.
Editing the output directly::The result box is read-only; change the input instead.
page.limits:
Input must be valid JSON; comments and trailing commas fail.
The tool validates but does not repair broken JSON.
No schema validation or type inspection is performed.
Very large documents may be slow to display in the result pane.
page.faqs:
Why does valid-looking JSON fail?::Common causes are trailing commas, single-quoted strings, comments and missing closing brackets. JSON requires double quotes around keys and string values, and it has no comment syntax. Fix the reported location in the input, then click Format again.
What is the difference between Format and Minify?::Format adds indentation and line breaks so the structure is easy to read. Minify removes optional whitespace to produce the shortest valid form. Both parse the same input and reject the same errors; only the written output changes.
Does the tool repair broken JSON?::No. It reports the parser message and clears the output when parsing fails. Use the message to find the first syntax problem, edit the input and run again. Automatic repair would change your data in ways you might not intend.
Will key order change?::JavaScript preserves the order of object keys as they appear in the parsed text, so the formatted output keeps that order. Numbers, booleans and null stay as values. Whitespace is the only thing the formatter intentionally changes.
Can I format JSON with Unicode text?::Yes. Parsing and stringifying preserve Unicode characters in string values, including emoji and non-Latin scripts. Escaped sequences stay escaped when present in the input. The monospace result pane makes it easier to spot misplaced quotes.
Is this JSON formatter free and private?::Yes. There is no sign-up and no upload. Parsing happens in the browser, so payloads with internal data stay on your device. Copy the cleaned text when you are ready and close the tab when you are done.
page.trustBody: Documented by the Toolpika team. The two output modes and error message match the tool above. Content current as of 24 November 2026.

unit-converter.title: Unit Converter
unit-converter.shortDesc: Convert length, weight, temperature and more.

seo.title: Unit Converter - Length, Weight and Degrees
seo.description: Convert lengths, weights and temperatures with this unit converter as you type. Check temperature conversion or swap units, then read the result.

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: Unit Converter changes values between metres and feet, kilograms and pounds, or Celsius and Fahrenheit. Pick a category, enter a number, choose two units and read the answer straight away. The calculation happens locally, with no account and no data sent anywhere.
page.contextualLink: Need to rename the labels in a spreadsheet after converting? Try {tool}.
page.whatIs:
A unit converter translates a measurement from one scale to another. It multiplies or divides by a fixed factor, or, for temperature, shifts the zero point as well.

Length conversions use the metre as the base. One inch is exactly 0.0254 metres, one foot is 0.3048 metres and one mile is 1609.344 metres. Weight conversions use the gram as the base; one pound is exactly 453.59237 grams. Those fixed definitions are why conversions are repeatable.

Temperature is different because Celsius, Fahrenheit and kelvin do not share a zero point. The tool converts any input to Celsius first, then converts from Celsius to the target scale. Absolute zero is 0 kelvin, which equals minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.

You choose a category, enter a number and pick units from two lists. Results are formatted for your page language and show at most six decimal places. That limit keeps the answer readable, though it may round a repeating decimal. Swap units reverses the two selections without touching the number you entered.

The tool covers length, weight and temperature; currency and time are outside its scope. Each category starts with a practical default pair, such as metres to feet. Values entered in the field stay unchanged until you edit them yourself.
page.howTo:
Pick Length, Weight or Temperature in the input panel.
Enter a number in the Value field.
Choose units from the From and To lists.
Press Swap units to reverse the direction.
Read the converted number in the result panel.
page.exampleOutput:
100 c = 212 f
Formatted with up to six decimal places
page.exampleNote: Temperature conversion goes through Celsius, and this pair has an exact result.
page.features:
Three categories::Length, weight and temperature each have their own unit lists.
Live calculation::The result updates as soon as a value or unit changes.
Swap units::Reverse From and To with one button.
Localised numbers::Formatting follows the language of your page.
Six decimals::Results are rounded to at most six fractional digits.
page.useCases:
Convert metric recipes::Change grams to ounces or centimetres to inches.
Read weather data::Switch between Celsius and Fahrenheit.
Fill in forms::Convert a height from metres to feet before submitting.
Compare parcel weights::Change kilograms to pounds for a shipping quote.
page.mistakes:
Mixing category units::Switching category resets From and To to defaults.
Assuming exact Celsius conversions::Temperatures can show long decimals within six places.
Typing units into the value field::Enter the number only; pick units from the lists.
page.limits:
Only length, weight and temperature are supported.
Results show up to six decimal places.
No currency or time conversions are available.
Blank or non-numeric values show an empty result.
page.faqs:
Which units can I convert?::Length supports millimetres, centimetres, metres, kilometres, inches, feet, yards and miles. Weight supports milligrams, grams, kilograms, ounces and pounds. Temperature supports Celsius, Fahrenheit and kelvin. Each category has its own pair of lists.
How accurate are the results?::Conversions use fixed factors, including 0.3048 metres per foot and 453.59237 grams per pound. Temperature converts through Celsius. Results show at most six decimal places, so rounded values may hide tiny differences in long chains of conversions.
What does Swap units do?::It exchanges the From and To selections and leaves the numeric value in place. For example, a metre-to-feet conversion becomes feet-to-metres with the same entry. Click it again to return to the original direction.
Why did my units change when I picked a category?::Each category has a sensible default pair: metres to feet, kilograms to pounds and Celsius to Fahrenheit. Choosing another category resets both lists to that pair so the first result is useful. Set your own units afterwards.
Can I convert currency or time?::No. This tool covers length, weight and temperature only. Currency rates change constantly and would need a live data source, which this browser-only tool does not use. Use a dedicated converter for money or time zones.
Is the unit converter free to use?::Yes. It is free, runs in your browser and needs no account. Your numbers never leave the page, and there is nothing to install. Open it, enter a value and read the result whenever you need a quick conversion.
page.trustBody: Prepared by the Toolpika team. The three categories and unit lists match the tool above. Last reviewed 24 November 2026.

seo.title: Password Generator - Strong, Random Passwords
seo.description: Create strong credentials with this password generator using browser randomness. Set password length and groups, then copy a fresh secret now.

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: Password Generator creates random secrets with browser cryptography and lets you set length and character groups. Every click makes a fresh value, which you can copy in one step. Nothing is uploaded or stored, so you can generate credentials privately.
page.contextualLink: Turning a memorable phrase into a username? Normalise its spelling with {tool}.
page.whatIs:
A password generator builds a secret from random characters rather than from a word or phrase you choose. This tool uses browser cryptography as its random source and assembles the result locally.

You set a length between 8 and 64 characters and choose from four groups: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers and symbols. The symbol group includes characters such as exclamation marks, at signs and brackets. Each selected group contributes at least one character, and the final string is shuffled.

Look-alike characters are deliberately excluded. You will not see i, l, 1, L, o, 0 or O, which reduces mistakes when a password must be typed from a screen or read aloud. The remaining sets are still large enough for everyday account secrets.

Longer values are harder to guess by brute force, so length matters more than unusual characters. The strength label here is a simple rule: 16 characters with three groups shows Strong, 12 with two shows Good, and anything shorter shows Weak. Store the result in a password manager and use a different value for every account. Each click draws fresh randomness, so the previous password will not appear again on request. Keep the copied value somewhere safe before you move to another site.
page.howTo:
Set the Length slider between 8 and 64 characters.
Tick or untick Uppercase letters, Lowercase letters, Numbers and Symbols.
Click Generate to build a new password.
Check the length and strength shown under the result.
Copy the password or adjust options and generate again.
page.exampleInput:
Length: 20
Uppercase letters: on
Lowercase letters: on
Numbers: on
Symbols: on
page.exampleNote: Characters are random, so your generated password will differ each time.
page.features:
Browser randomness::Uses crypto.getRandomValues for every character.
Adjustable length::Slider runs from 8 to 64 characters.
Four character groups::Toggle uppercase, lowercase, numbers and symbols independently.
Guaranteed variety::When groups are selected, each contributes at least one character.
Strength label::Shows Weak, Good or Strong from length and group count.
Copy::Places the new password on your clipboard.
page.useCases:
Create a new account::Generate a unique secret for each service.
Replace a reused password::Make a fresh value after a breach notice.
Set up a device::Produce a long passphrase for a new laptop.
Test a signup flow::Fill password fields with a valid sample.
page.mistakes:
Reusing a password::Generate a new value for every service.
Turning off every group::No password is produced when all character groups are unticked.
Trusting the strength label alone::It reflects length and variety, not how you store the secret.
page.limits:
Length is limited to 8 through 64 characters.
Look-alike characters are removed from every character set.
Strength labels are simple rules, not a full security audit.
page.faqs:
How long should my password be?::Use the longest value the service accepts. The slider starts at 8 characters and goes to 64; 20 or more is a practical choice for new accounts. Length matters more than clever substitutions because each added character expands the search space.
Why are some letters missing?::The character sets leave out look-alike characters such as i, l, 1, L, o, 0 and O. That makes a password easier to read aloud or type from a screen. The remaining letters, numbers and symbols still provide plenty of variety.
What does the strength label mean?::It is a simple rule based on length and how many character groups you selected. At least 16 characters with three groups shows Strong; 12 with two groups shows Good. It does not measure how safely you store or share the password.
Does every selected group appear?::Yes. The generator picks one character from each selected group, then fills the remaining positions from the combined pool. It shuffles the result so the required characters are not always first. Turn off all groups and generation produces nothing.
Can I get the same password again?::No. Each click draws fresh values from browser randomness, so the previous password is not repeated on demand. Copy it to a password manager straight away. If you lose it, generate a new one and replace the old secret.
Is this generator private?::Yes. Passwords are built in your browser with the Web Crypto API and are never transmitted or stored. Nothing is logged, and a refresh starts with an empty result. Generate, copy and save the value wherever you keep your credentials.
page.trustBody: Created by the Toolpika team. The four character groups and length range match the tool above. This page was updated on 24 November 2026.

url-encoder.title: URL Encoder / Decoder
url-encoder.shortDesc: Encode or decode URLs and query strings.

seo.title: URL Encoder - Encode and Decode Query Strings
seo.description: Prepare safe links with this URL encoder that also decodes escaped text. Encode a query string, check the result, then copy it into your request.

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: URL Encoder escapes text for use inside web addresses and reverses escaped values when you need them back. Paste a value, click Encode or Decode, then copy the exact result. Everything runs in your browser with no account and no upload step.

page.whatIs:
A URL encoder converts text into a form that can travel safely inside a web address. This tool applies component encoding, replacing characters that have a special meaning in URLs with a percent sign followed by two hexadecimal digits.

A space becomes %20. A colon becomes %3A, a slash %2F, a question mark %3F and an ampersand %26. Letters, digits and a small set of safe symbols are left alone. The result is one escaped string rather than a working link.

The distinction matters. A full URL needs its slashes and colon to remain unescaped so a browser can find the host and path. Component encoding is meant for individual pieces, such as a search phrase or a query value, which are then placed into a URL built by your application.

Decoding reverses the process. The tool checks that every percent escape is well formed and reports an error when it is not. It does not fetch the address, shorten links or validate that a host exists. Use it when preparing request parameters, reading logs or debugging a redirect. Decoded output is plain text you can copy back into a form or a piece of code. Plus signs are escaped too, which differs from older form-style encoding.
page.howToTitle: How to use URL Encoder / Decoder
page.howTo:
Paste a URL or query string into the Text box.
Click Encode to escape spaces and special characters.
Click Decode to turn escaped text back into readable form.
Copy the result or Clear both boxes to start again.
page.exampleNote: Encoding a complete URL escapes its slashes; encode values separately for links.
page.features:
Encode button::Escapes a value with encodeURIComponent rules.
Decode button::Reverses percent escapes when the input is well formed.
Error message::Invalid escapes show a short explanation instead of a result.
Copy and clear::Take the output or reset both boxes.
Monospace view::Read escaped strings without font ambiguity.
page.useCasesTitle: When to use URL Encoder / Decoder
page.useCases:
Build query strings::Escape a search phrase before adding it to a link.
Debug API calls::Decode a returned value to read its original text.
Share exact links::Encode parameters that contain spaces or ampersands.
Inspect logs::Decode percent escapes from a recorded URL.
page.mistakes:
Encoding a whole URL::Component encoding escapes slashes too; use it for values, not ready-made links.
Decoding twice::Decode once; repeated decoding can corrupt percent signs.
Expecting form-style encoding::Spaces become %20 here, not plus signs.
page.limits:
Uses component encoding, so a whole URL becomes one escaped string.
No URL shortening, validation or fetching is performed.
Invalid percent escapes fail when decoding.
page.faqs:
What does Encode actually change?::It applies component encoding: spaces become %20, and characters such as colon, slash, question mark and ampersand become percent escapes. Letters, digits and a few safe symbols stay as they are. The result is a single escaped string, not a clickable URL.
Why is my encoded URL not opening?::Encoding a complete URL escapes its slashes and colon, so browsers treat it as one value rather than an address. Encode only the parameter value you plan to insert, or paste the decoded link into your browser instead.
When should I click Decode?::Use Decode when you receive text with percent escapes, such as a value from a log or an API response. The tool converts valid escapes back into readable characters. If an escape is incomplete, you see an error instead of a broken result.
Does it handle plus signs?::Spaces are encoded as %20 rather than the plus sign used by older form encoding. A plus sign in your input is escaped as %2B and decodes back to a plus. Check which convention the service you are calling expects before you paste.
Can I encode a whole query string at once?::You can, but every reserved character will be escaped, including the equals signs that separate keys from values. For a usable link, encode each value on its own and assemble the query string afterwards with plain separators.
Is the URL encoder free and private?::Yes. Encoding and decoding run locally in your browser with no account and no upload. Anything you paste stays in the tab until you clear it. Copy the result when it looks right and carry on with your request.
page.trustBody: Explained by the Toolpika team. The Encode and Decode buttons and error message match the tool above. Current to 24 November 2026.

seo.title: Base64 Encoder - Encode and Decode Any Text
seo.description: Turn text into Base64 with this Base64 encoder that also handles decoding. Decode Base64 from an API field or encode your own string, then copy the result.

page.byline: By the Toolpika team · Last updated 24 November 2026
page.directAnswer: Base64 Encoder converts UTF-8 text into standard Base64 and decodes Base64 strings back into text. Paste a value, choose Encode or Decode, and copy the output. Processing stays in your browser, so nothing leaves your device and no sign-up is required.
page.contextualLink: Preparing a text value for encoding? Standardise its style first with {tool}.
page.whatIs:
A Base64 encoder represents text as a sequence of 64 printable characters. It is an encoding, not encryption: anyone can reverse it without a key. This tool converts between ordinary UTF-8 text and standard Base64 in your browser.

Encoding first turns text into bytes using UTF-8, then groups those bytes in threes. Each three-byte group becomes four output characters from the alphabet of letters, digits, plus and slash. When the input length is not a multiple of three, one or two equals signs pad the end.

Decoding performs the reverse. This tool removes whitespace before checking the alphabet, so wrapped strings from emails or logs work. It rejects characters outside the standard alphabet, including the minus and underscore used by URL-safe Base64.

Base64 appears in data URLs, email attachments, JSON fields and HTTP headers because it keeps binary-safe bytes in a text-only form. It makes payloads about one third larger, so it is not a compression method. Never use it to conceal secrets. Encoding preserves emoji and non-Latin scripts because the byte conversion starts with UTF-8. Copy the result directly from the output box when you need it in another system. Decoding an invalid string leaves the result empty and shows a short error.
page.howToTitle: How to use Base64 Encoder / Decoder
page.howTo:
Paste text into the Text box on the left.
Click Encode to convert it to Base64 characters.
Click Decode to check a Base64 string from elsewhere.
Copy the result or Clear both boxes for a new string.

page.features:
Encode button::Converts UTF-8 text to standard Base64.
Decode button::Turns Base64 text back into UTF-8 characters.
Whitespace tolerance::Decoding ignores spaces and line breaks.
Invalid input flag::Rejects characters outside the standard Base64 alphabet.
Copy and clear::Move the result to your clipboard or start again.
page.useCasesTitle: When to use Base64 Encoder / Decoder
page.useCases:
Prepare API payloads::Encode text for a field that expects Base64.
Read encoded tokens::Decode a value pasted from a response.
Check sample data::Round-trip a string to confirm an encoding step.
Clean embedded strings::Encode text that must avoid line breaks.
page.mistakes:
Calling Base64 encryption::Anyone can decode it; never use it to hide secrets.
Pasting URL-safe Base64::Minus and underscore are rejected; convert to standard Base64 first.
Ignoring whitespace rules::Decoding strips whitespace, but other invalid characters still fail.
page.limits:
Handles UTF-8 text, not arbitrary binary file uploads.
Decoding accepts standard Base64 with optional whitespace.
URL-safe Base64 with - and _ is rejected.
Base64 is an encoding, never a way to secure data.
page.faqs:
Is Base64 encryption?::No. Base64 is an encoding scheme that represents bytes with 64 printable characters. Anyone can decode it without a key, so never use it to hide passwords or private data. Use proper encryption when confidentiality matters.
Why does my encoded text end with equals signs?::Base64 works in groups of three bytes. When input length is not a multiple of three, padding characters are added so the last group is complete. One or two equals signs at the end are normal and are removed again when you decode.
Can I decode a string with line breaks?::Yes. Decoding removes spaces and line breaks before checking the alphabet, so wrapped Base64 from an email or log usually works. Characters outside the standard set, such as minus or underscore, still cause an error.
Does it support emoji and other scripts?::Yes. Encoding converts text to UTF-8 bytes first, so emoji and non-Latin characters survive a round trip. Decoding rebuilds the same characters from those bytes. Keep the original text if you need to know how it looked before encoding.
Why does my long text produce one long line?::Base64 output has no line breaks by design, which makes it easy to paste into headers and JSON fields. The result box wraps visually without changing the value. Copy always takes the single unbroken string.
Is the Base64 encoder free and private?::Yes. Encoding and decoding happen in your browser with no sign-up and no upload. Your text is not sent anywhere or stored after you leave. Paste, choose an action, copy the result and close the tab when you are finished.
page.trustBody: Supported by the Toolpika team. The standard Base64 alphabet and UTF-8 handling match the tool above. Checked on 24 November 2026.

page.whatIsTitle: What is JSON to CSV conversion?
page.whatIs:
JSON stores data as nested key-value records, while CSV stores the same records as rows and columns. Conversion maps each object to a row and each top-level key to a column.

This tool expects tabular JSON: an array of similar objects or an object whose values are objects. Arrays and nested objects inside a cell are flattened with dot paths so the table stays predictable.

page.howTo:

page.exampleNote: The column order follows the first object. Later objects may add or omit keys; missing keys produce empty cells.
page.features:

Delimiter choice::Comma, semicolon and tab output are supported.
Header control::Include or omit the column-name row.

Can I import CSV back to JSON?::This page focuses on JSON to CSV. Use a dedicated CSV parser if you need strict reverse conversion with schema control.
How are commas inside values handled?::Values containing commas, quotes or newlines are wrapped in double quotes, with inner quotes doubled, following RFC 4180 conventions.
page.trustBody: The conversion uses only browser APIs. No account, upload or network request is involved, and clearing the page removes your input.

Markdown is a plain-text shorthand for headings, emphasis, lists and links. HTML is the markup a browser actually renders. Conversion translates the shorthand into semantic tags.

This converter supports a practical subset of CommonMark. It escapes raw HTML before parsing, which means a pasted script tag becomes text instead of executable markup.

page.whatIsTitle: What are HEX, RGB and HSL?
page.whatIs:
HEX writes a color as hexadecimal red, green and blue channels. RGB writes the same channels as decimal numbers from 0 to 255. HSL describes hue, saturation and lightness, which is often easier to adjust by eye.

All three describe the same sRGB color. This converter parses one format and calculates the other two, rounding only at the final display step.

Channel validation::RGB values outside 0-255 are rejected.

Quick copy::Each output format has its own copy button.

Write CSS::Move a design value into a stylesheet.
Build tokens::Keep a design system in one canonical format.
Tune palettes::Adjust lightness without guessing hex digits.
Debug styles::Compare a computed color with its source value.

Mixing syntaxes::Missing # on hex or % on HSL values causes an error.

page.whatIs:
A base defines how many digit symbols a numbering system uses. Decimal has ten, binary has two, octal has eight and hexadecimal has sixteen.

The same quantity can be written in any base. Programmers switch bases to match machine representations, bit masks or compact notation, while the underlying value stays unchanged.

Why do I get an invalid-digit error?::Each base has a fixed digit set. Octal accepts 0-7 and hexadecimal accepts 0-9 plus A-F; anything else cannot represent a value in that base.
Can I paste a prefixed value?::Yes. Prefixes such as 0b, 0o and 0x are recognised case-insensitively and are removed before conversion.
How large can the number be?::The tool uses BigInt, so it is limited by available memory rather than by JavaScript's safe-integer range.

page.whatIs:
A Unix timestamp counts seconds since 1 January 1970 at 00:00 UTC. Many APIs also use milliseconds, which are the same count multiplied by one thousand.

Because the count is timezone-independent, it is a reliable way to store an instant. Displaying it still requires a timezone, which is why this tool shows both UTC and your local time.

page.whatIsTitle: Why are there two storage unit systems?
page.whatIs:
Storage vendors use SI units where one kilobyte is 1000 bytes. Operating systems often use IEC units where one kibibyte is 1024 bytes. The labels look similar, but the underlying factors differ.

That difference grows with scale: a one-terabyte drive shows less usable space when a system reports it in tebibytes. This converter makes the chosen system explicit.

Choose the target unit from the second selector.
Use swap to reverse the direction, then copy the result.

page.features:
Both systems::SI units from B to TB and IEC units up to TiB.
Swap direction::Reverse source and target with one click.
Locale formatting::Numbers use your browser's locale rules.
Clear errors::Negative or non-numeric input is rejected early.
page.useCases:
Check disk space::Compare a drive label with an operating-system reading.
Plan uploads::Estimate how many files fit into a quota.
Read specs::Translate vendor numbers into binary units.
Explain warnings::Show why reported sizes differ between tools.
page.mistakes:
Assuming KB means 1024 bytes::That is KiB in the IEC system.
Mixing systems mid-calculation::Pick one factor for the whole conversion.
Entering negative sizes::Storage quantities cannot be negative.
page.limits:
Bits and byte-rate units such as megabits per second are not included.
Results are rounded for display, not for exact accounting.
Very large values use floating-point math and may lose precision.
page.faqs:
Why does my drive show less space than advertised?::Manufacturers count in powers of ten, while many operating systems count in powers of two. A 1 TB drive is about 0.91 TiB, so the reported number looks smaller even though nothing is missing.
What does KiB mean?::KiB is the IEC symbol for kibibyte, which is 1024 bytes. KB usually means kilobyte, or 1000 bytes, in the SI system.
Can I convert gigabits to gigabytes?::Not here. This tool covers storage amounts rather than transfer rates; divide bits by eight first if you need bytes.
Does the result use my locale?::Yes. The displayed number follows your browser locale through Intl.NumberFormat, so grouping separators feel familiar.
page.trustBody: Calculations happen locally. No value is uploaded or retained.

seo.description: Create URL-safe slugs from headings and titles. Choose a separator, strip accents and punctuation, and copy the result as you type.

page.directAnswer: Turn headings and titles into clean URL slugs. Choose a hyphen or underscore separator, strip accents and punctuation, and copy the result. The preview updates as you type so you can spot duplicate or overly long slugs early before publishing.
page.contextualLink: A good slug starts with clean source text; %%TOOL%% helps tidy the heading first.
page.whatIsTitle: What makes a good URL slug?
page.whatIs:
A slug is the readable part of a URL that identifies a page. Good slugs are short, lowercase, stable and free of characters that need encoding.

This generator normalises Unicode accents, removes punctuation, collapses whitespace and joins words with your chosen separator, producing a value you can paste into a CMS or route definition.
page.howTo:
Paste a title or heading into the input box.
Pick a hyphen or underscore separator.
Choose whether accents should be stripped.
Copy the generated slug and check it in your CMS.
page.exampleNote: Accents are transliterated when stripping is enabled, and symbols such as ampersands are removed.
page.features:
Lowercase output::All letters are normalised to lower case.
Separator choice::Hyphens or underscores in one click.
Accent stripping::Diacritics become plain ASCII letters.
Punctuation cleanup::Extra symbols and whitespace are collapsed.
page.useCases:
Publish posts::Create stable addresses for new articles.
Name docs pages::Keep documentation URLs readable.
Plan redirects::Compare old and new slugs before migration.
Avoid duplicates::Spot collisions across a content calendar.
page.mistakes:
Changing slugs after publishing::Existing links may break without redirects.
Keeping stop words::Very long slugs are harder to read and share.
Mixing separators::One convention per site keeps URLs predictable.
page.limits:
Non-Latin scripts without diacritics are preserved as-is rather than transliterated.
Emoji are removed rather than encoded.
Length is not truncated automatically.
page.faqs:
What happens to accented letters?::With accent stripping enabled, the text is normalised and diacritics are removed, so café becomes cafe. Turn the option off to keep the original characters.
Why was punctuation removed?::Characters such as ampersands, colons and exclamation marks either need URL encoding or add noise. Removing them produces a cleaner, more stable address.
Can I use underscores instead of hyphens?::Yes. Choose the underscore separator and every word boundary becomes an underscore. Pick one style and use it consistently across your site.
Does the tool shorten long slugs?::No. It keeps the full phrase so you can decide which words matter. Trim the source text if you need a shorter address.
page.trustBody: Slug creation happens in your browser. No title is logged or uploaded.

yaml-to-json.title: YAML to JSON Converter
yaml-to-json.shortDesc: Convert YAML configuration into formatted JSON.

seo.title: YAML to JSON Converter - Indentation-Safe Output
seo.description: Convert common YAML maps and lists into formatted JSON. Clear indentation errors, configurable spacing and local-only processing.

yaml-to-json.invalidYaml: That YAML could not be parsed. Check indentation and quotes.
yaml-to-json.unsupported: YAML anchors and custom tags are not supported.

page.directAnswer: Convert YAML configuration into formatted JSON you can paste into an API or app. The parser handles indentation, lists, numbers and booleans, then reports the exact line that failed. Nothing is uploaded; the conversion runs locally in your browser tab.
page.contextualLink: If you need a structured table from the result, %%TOOL%% can flatten the records.
page.whatIs:
YAML is a human-readable data format that uses indentation instead of braces. It is common in configuration files, while JSON is more widely accepted by APIs and JavaScript tools.

This converter reads a practical YAML subset: maps, lists, quoted and plain strings, numbers, booleans and null. It does not evaluate tags or anchors.
page.howToTitle: How to convert YAML to JSON
page.howTo:
Paste YAML into the input panel.
Choose two or four spaces for the JSON indent.
Read the formatted JSON on the right.
Copy it or download it as a .json file.
page.exampleNote: Quoted values stay strings, while bare true, false, null and numbers become JSON literals.
page.features:
Nested maps::Indented keys become nested JSON objects.
Lists::Block sequences become JSON arrays.
Scalar types::Numbers, booleans and null are detected.
Indent control::Two or four space output.
page.useCasesTitle: When to convert YAML to JSON
page.useCases:
Configure apps::Move a config file into a JSON-based tool.
Call APIs::Prepare a request body from YAML notes.
Compare formats::Inspect how a config maps to JSON.
Validate data::Spot indentation mistakes before deployment.
page.mistakes:
Using tabs::YAML requires spaces for indentation.
Mixing indentation levels::Sibling keys must align exactly.
Expecting anchors::References and custom tags are not resolved.
page.limits:
Multiline block scalars are treated as plain text.
Complex keys and merge keys are outside the subset.
Very large documents may render slowly in the browser.
page.faqs:
Why did my file fail to parse?::Most failures come from tabs or inconsistent indentation. Make sure sibling keys align at the same column and that nested values are indented further.
Are booleans and numbers converted?::Yes. Bare true, false, null and numeric values become the matching JSON types, while quoted values stay strings.
Can I reuse anchors and aliases?::No. Anchors, aliases and custom tags are deliberately unsupported so the parser stays deterministic and safe.
Is my configuration uploaded?::No. Parsing and formatting happen entirely in your browser, and nothing is stored after you close the page.
page.trustBody: The parser runs locally with no network access. Your configuration stays on this device.

about.title: About Toolpika
about.description: Toolpika is a collection of small utilities that run in your browser.
about.intro: Toolpika is a collection of small utilities. Each does one job, without asking you to sign up.
about.privacyBody: Every tool that touches a file or text processes it inside your browser. Nothing is uploaded, so we never see your content.
about.contactBody: Mail us and a human replies.
about.perkInstantBody: Every tool opens in a tab and works the moment you load it.
about.perkSmallBody: One job per tool, so there is nothing to learn before you begin.
about.believeTitle: Useful tools should stay out of the way.
about.believeBody: No accounts, no uploads and no clutter. Just a quiet collection of utilities that do one job well and leave when you are done.
about.storyTitle: Built for the small jobs, every day.
about.storyBody1: Toolpika started as a set of private utilities for everyday work. Each one solved a single annoyance without asking for a sign-up or sending a file to a server.
about.storyBody2: That idea still drives the site. Tools stay local, pages stay light and the collection grows only when something is genuinely useful.
about.specificBody: Tell us what you need and we will look at it. We read every request.

privacy.filesBody: Tools that accept files run entirely in your browser using the File and Canvas APIs. File contents are never sent to a server and are never stored.
privacy.dataBody: We do not require an account. We store your theme and language preference in your browser's local storage, which never leaves your device.
privacy.cookiesBody: Toolpika does not set tracking cookies. A single essential cookie may be used to remember your language preference.

privacy.dataList2: No account is required to use any public tool.
